evals.name: bare-invocation-stays-read-only
evals.expected_output: Fetches the current prompting-guide pages, inventories locally-owned instruction components, classifies each by purpose, judges only the postures whose predicates match, and produces a report of MISSING/PRESENT/NOT-APPLICABLE verdicts with proposed additions as diffs, persisted to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA. It never edits a component: proposals are artifacts the human applies, and a clean audit (all PRESENT or NOT-APPLICABLE) is a valid, expected outcome.
expectations: Fetches the guide pages live before judging; proposal wording comes from the fetch, not the catalog
Produces a report with proposed additions and does not Edit or Write any audited component
Defaults to NOT-APPLICABLE where a posture's predicate does not match the component's purpose, rather than manufacturing findings

evals.name: routes-present-and-wrong-text-out
evals.prompt: /claude-config:audit-prompting-postures my skill says 'CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool' — should that change?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that judging existing instruction text (over-aggressive emphasis is audit-instructions' I28) is out of this skill's scope and routes to claude-config:audit-instructions, rather than proposing a rewrite itself. This skill owns only absent-and-needed posture guidance.
expectations: Routes present-and-wrong instruction text to claude-config:audit-instructions
Does not propose a rewrite of existing text under this skill's own contract

evals.name: human-gated-design-not-flagged
evals.prompt: /claude-config:audit-prompting-postures skills — one of my skills is report-only and always ends by asking the user to approve findings; is it missing an autonomy posture?
evals.expected_output: Applies P6's predicate correctly: a report-only flow ending at a human gate is NOT-APPLICABLE for the autonomy posture — the posture binds components that claim unattended operation. The skill reports NOT-APPLICABLE with the failed predicate rather than proposing an autonomous-pipeline branch.
expectations: Judges P6 NOT-APPLICABLE for a report-only, human-gated component
Names the failed predicate in the verdict instead of manufacturing a finding

evals.name: two-roots-produce-two-reports
evals.prompt: /claude-config:audit-prompting-postures — I ran this in my work repo yesterday and I am running it in a different repo now. Will today's run overwrite yesterday's report, and where does each land?
evals.expected_output: No. The report path carries a state key derived per project — <repo-identity>/<worktree-discriminator>, the scheme audit-pass already uses — so the two runs write to different directories under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/audit-prompting-postures/ and both survive. The skill derives the key by RUNNING the documented commands (git remote, git toplevel, sha256 of the canonicalized root), not by testing whether a placeholder is set. It names a distinct resolved path for each run, and notes that two worktrees of the SAME repository also key apart because the discriminator hashes the worktree root.
expectations: Answers that the second run does NOT overwrite the first, and names a distinct path for each
Derives the state key by running the documented git and sha256 commands rather than by evaluating whether a placeholder is set
Reuses audit-pass's <repo-identity>/<worktree-discriminator> scheme rather than inventing a second keying scheme
States that two worktrees of one repository also key apart, via the worktree discriminator

evals.name: non-repo-root-still-keys-and-self-describes
evals.prompt: /claude-config:audit-prompting-postures — I am running this from my home directory, which is not a git repository at all. Does it still work, and can I tell later which root a saved report came from?
evals.expected_output: Yes to both. The identity ladder carries a third rung for a non-repo root — nonrepo/<hash of the working directory> — because this skill is report-only and legitimately audits such roots, unlike audit-pass which refuses non-git targets outright. And the report opens with a mandated three-line header giving the resolved root, the scope filter, and a UTC timestamp, so a surviving file is self-describing rather than merely un-overwritten.
expectations: Runs rather than refusing, and keys the report under a non-repo rung instead of falling back to one fixed shared path
Does NOT invent a git-only derivation that cannot resolve without a repository
States that the report opens with a header naming the resolved root, the scope filter, and a UTC timestamp

evals.name: description-drives-selection-without-explicit-invocation
evals.prompt: I just wrote a new orchestrator skill that fans out to subagents. What guardrails is it missing that the official prompting guide says a skill like that should carry?
evals.expected_output: This skill is selected from its description alone — the request carries no slash invocation — because it asks for guidance that is ABSENT and needed, which is this skill's lane rather than audit-instructions', whose lane is text that is present and wrong. It classifies the component as orchestrating, judges P1 (delegation criteria and caps) and any other posture whose predicate actually matches, sources proposed wording from a live fetch of the prompting guide rather than from the catalog, and returns proposals for the human to apply.
expectations: Handled by audit-prompting-postures with no slash command typed, and NOT routed to claude-config:audit-instructions, which owns present-and-wrong text rather than absent-and-needed guidance
Classifies the component as orchestrating and judges P1, rather than sweeping all ten postures regardless of predicate
Proposed wording comes from a live fetch of the guide, not from reference/postures.md, which carries pointers only
Proposes rather than applies: no component file is edited

evals.name: mechanical-gate-counts-as-p7-presence
evals.prompt: /claude-config:audit-prompting-postures skills — my deploy skill can force-push and carries no confirmation wording anywhere in its body, but a PreToolUse hook denies the push unless the operator approves it. Is it MISSING P7?
evals.expected_output: No. P7's own 'present when' says a deny-by-default hook or script gate satisfies it without any prose, so the hook is presence evidence and the verdict is PRESENT, cited to the hook configuration and the rule. Phase B's inventory covers instruction text and therefore cannot hold that evidence, which is why Phase C looks for the gate in the settings scopes and hook configuration before judging P7 MISSING — and widening the evidence set that way can only turn a MISSING into a PRESENT, never create a finding.
expectations: Returns PRESENT for P7, not MISSING, and cites the hook as the evidence
States that mechanical gates are presence evidence living outside Phase B's instruction-text inventory
Does not extend the mechanical-gate allowance to postures other than P7
Does not treat mere Bash access as satisfying the destructive-capable predicate
